# windows_timezone (Resource)

Manages the system time zone of a remote Windows machine over SSH/PowerShell.

The system time zone is a **singleton**: the host always has exactly one, so creating this resource never provisions anything new — it only sets the zone in place (`Set-TimeZone`, or `tzutil.exe /s "<id>_dstoff"` when `daylight_saving_disabled` is true), and deleting it makes no remote change unless `restore_on_destroy` is set.

Windows time zone IDs are used (e.g. `Romance Standard Time`); IANA IDs such as `Europe/Paris` are rejected at plan time. The Terraform resource ID is anchored on `id` (HKLM `MachineGuid`), not on the zone, so it survives zone changes.

When the `tzautoupdate` service may change the zone automatically (`tzautoupdate_enabled`), every operation warns: Windows can move the zone out from under Terraform.

**Destroy is a no-op by default:** a Windows machine cannot exist without a time zone; `terraform destroy` only removes the resource from state unless `restore_on_destroy` re-applies the pre-existing zone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: set the target host's system time zone to UTC.
# The zone is a singleton — this resource sets it in place and never
# provisions anything new. Destroy is a no-op unless restore_on_destroy
# re-applies the pre-existing zone captured at creation time.
resource "windows_timezone" "this" {
  timezone_id        = "UTC"
  restore_on_destroy = true

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly: without this block each
  # operation defaults to 5 minutes, and a stalled Set-TimeZone or read-back
  # surfaces a timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform
  # indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "5m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "5m"
    delete = "5m"
  }
}

output "timezone_id" {
  value       = windows_timezone.this.timezone_id
  description = "Configured Windows time zone ID."
}

output "current_utc_offset" {
  value       = windows_timezone.this.current_utc_offset
  description = "Live effective UTC offset (base plus the active DST delta, if any)."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `timezone_id` (String) Windows time zone ID (e.g. `Romance Standard Time`). Windows IDs never contain `/`; IANA IDs such as `Europe/Paris` are not supported — use the Windows ID instead. Comparison is **case-insensitive**.

### Optional

- `daylight_saving_disabled` (Boolean) When `true`, daylight saving time is disabled for the zone (`tzutil.exe /s "<id>_dstoff"`). Default: `false`.
- `restore_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, destroy re-applies the pre-existing time zone values captured at creation (or import) time. Defaults to `false`: destroy makes no remote change.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `base_utc_offset` (String) Standard (non-DST) UTC offset of the zone, formatted as `+HH:mm` (e.g. `+01:00`).
- `current_utc_offset` (String) Live effective UTC offset (base plus the active DST delta, if any), formatted as `+HH:mm` (e.g. `+02:00` in summer).
- `display_name` (String) Localized display name of the configured time zone (e.g. `(UTC+01:00) Brussels, Copenhagen, Madrid, Paris`).
- `id` (String) Terraform resource ID. Equal to the host `MachineGuid` (`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid`). Stable across time zone changes.
- `supports_daylight_saving_time` (Boolean) Whether the zone definition includes daylight saving time.
- `tzautoupdate_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the `tzautoupdate` service may change the time zone automatically. When `true`, every operation warns that Windows can move the zone out from under Terraform.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the live system time zone of the target Windows host.
# The zone is a singleton, so any non-empty import ID is accepted and ignored:
# the live zone is adopted and becomes the snapshot for a later
# restore_on_destroy.
terraform import windows_timezone.this current
```
